description: Contextual keywords are legal binder and `local` BINDING names: `for empty in ...`, `for member from ... to ...`, and `local of` all bind ordinary names. They are structural by POSITION only -- just after `is` for all four, and additionally in the Heritage `value of ... for key` reader for `of` (spec/grammar.md:382) -- and a binder or `local` name is neither of those. Their reads resolve. No ol-reserved-word: these four are not built-in names, and since maintainer ruling #833 (issue #837) no binding position raises it for any name, `local` included, because `local` is not one of the grammar's four declaration slots (spec/grammar.md:384,390). No undefined-variable diagnostic either, so check() reports an empty stream. The carve-out specific to these four is proven at the DECLARATION slot by contextual-keyword-as-procedure-name.
